_what: The OBSERVING SITE for this rig, in the industry-standard keys. Every acquisition record derives its `site` block from this file, so the fact is rebuildable from a tracked file rather than living in a chat message or a machine-local config (CLAUDE.md, Environment: a machine-local value nobody can rebuild has already cost this repo a shipped optical model).
_standard: SITELAT / SITELONG / SITEELEV are SIRIL's own header keys, verified present in the installed 1.4.4 binary, so a value written here round-trips through the tool that consumes it. OBSGEO-X/Y/Z is the FITS-standard geocentric form (WCS Paper III; FITS 4.0 sec 8.4) and is DERIVED from the three above, never entered by hand. Both are emitted: the Siril keys because the toolchain reads them, the OBSGEO triple because it is the standard other software expects.
_override: A session shot somewhere else overrides this with datasets/<session>/site.json in the same schema. There is no silent default: a session with neither file gets a null site block that says so, and nothing downstream may assume a location.
sign_convention: SITELONG is POSITIVE EAST of Greenwich, which is the FITS and Siril convention and the OPPOSITE of the one some planetarium software uses. This site is in New Jersey, USA, so the value is NEGATIVE. A sign error here is silent and inverts every hour angle derived from it.
TRAP_if_you_ever_re_derive_this_from_a_m: In a Google Maps URL the `@lat,lon` segment is the map VIEWPORT CENTRE, not the place, and it is the segment that LOOKS like the coordinates so it is the one people reach for. MEASURED here: the viewport pair (REDACTED_SITELONG_VIEWPORT) and the place pair (REDACTED_SITELONG) differ by 219 m in longitude. The authoritative pair is `!3d<lat>!4d<lon>`.

provenance.source: owner-supplied ground truth, from two of their own sources that agree to 4 m
provenance.chain: owner -> chat -> peer-session transcription -> BACKLOG.md (corrected at commit f49b7cc, first landed at 4686cec) -> this file
provenance.why_that_matters: the chain still ends in a human typing a number, and no step in it has an independent check. A coordinate typo is silent and load-bearing — it propagates into every altitude, hour angle and parallactic angle derived downstream. Treat the value as provisional until the derivation below runs.
provenance.a_transcription_error_ALREADY_HAPPENED_H: the first landed value was SITELAT +REDACTED_SITELAT, SITELONG REDACTED_SITELONG, read off the owner's DMS as REDACTED_SITE_DMS_LON. The authoritative decimal pair reads 45.70", so the longitude was out by 0.17 arcsec = 3.918 m, and the latitude by 0.111 m. It changes nothing measured — aug06/set-01 altitude moves by 0.00003 deg — and it is recorded because of HOW it was caught: re-reading the same transcription did not find it, a second independent source did. That is the argument for the derivation, not for more careful reading.
provenance.the_check_that_closes_it: the corpus can RECOVER the latitude without any of this: field rotation between two solved frames constrains cos(lat)*cos(azimuth)*sec(altitude), so latitude and LST are solvable from solved RA/Dec plus DATE-OBS across several pointings on two nights. A derived-vs-supplied comparison verifies the transcription AND gives the derivation a positive control at the same time. NOT YET RUN — it needs PER-FRAME plate solves, which do not exist yet, so it is a real build rather than a fold-in. Until it runs, `verified` stays false.

bounding_check_that_HAS_run.what_it_is: a FALSIFICATION against 23 solved products carrying DATE-OBS and a plate-solved centre, not a derivation. It asks whether the supplied coordinates put the photographed targets where a deliberate observing plan would.
bounding_check_that_HAS_run.result: every target lands 63.4-87.7 deg above the horizon within 2.35 h of the meridian, and 2 of 5 plausible transcription errors are REFUTED outright by putting a photographed target BELOW the horizon (longitude sign flipped, -7.8 deg; lat/long transposed, -50.2 deg). A shifted decimal shows up as a 35.1 deg altitude shift.
bounding_check_that_HAS_run.THE_LIMIT_read_this_before_quoting_the_r: it has NO power against sub-degree digit errors. MEASURED: transposing a digit in the latitude (REDACTED_SITELAT -> REDACTED_SITELAT_PLUS, a 0.63 deg error) moves every altitude by only 0.29 deg, and the same in the longitude by 0.07 deg. So this bounds the transcription at roughly the DEGREE level and no better, which is why it does not set `verified`.
bounding_check_that_HAS_run.EVERY_NUMBER_IN_THIS_BLOCK_IS_READ_FROM: scripts/setup/site_verification.json, which verify_site.py regenerates. Quote it from there and re-sync this prose when the script re-runs: this block previously carried eight values that no longer matched the record it describes (20 products, 86.2 deg, 2.37 h, -5.7, -52.3, 35.6, 0.53, and the pre-correction latitude REDACTED_SITELAT), and a prose copy that drifts from its own generated record is worse than no copy, because it reads as independent confirmation.

siteelev_note: UNRECORDED, and deliberately left so rather than silently defaulted — a quietly assumed value is the machine-local-value problem in a different costume. What it is FOR, so a future reader can judge whether to chase it: elevation enters refraction and airmass, both weakly, and this corpus's refraction branch is already closed on the regime (every night shot 63.4-87.7 deg above the horizon, within 2.35 h of the meridian, where the curve is flat). So a nominal figure WITH ITS SOURCE STATED would be sufficient for anything currently on the board; nothing here needs a surveyed one. Until one is recorded, `siteelev_m` stays null and the derived OBSGEO triple is computed at h = 0 m with `siteelev_assumed_zero_for_obsgeo` set true in every record. The resulting geocentric error is at most the true elevation in metres (order 1e-5 of Earth's radius) — negligible for altitude, hour angle and field rotation, and NOT negligible for anything needing true topocentric parallax.
_what_is_deliberately_not_here: The owner also supplied a street address. It is not recorded, here or anywhere in the tree: nothing in the chain consumes it, and a tracked file carries what the measurement needs and no more.
